principles: The errata ledger is required evidence: its rows decide whether a defect is corrected, and an unmatched ledger row is itself a failure verdict.

A committed ledger whose blob object is unavailable locally is missing evidence, not an absent ledger: the auditor must exit 2 (could-not-evaluate), never fall back to an empty ledger and emit a verdict.
An absent ledger fallback converts missing evidence into a verdict. In the zero-defect arms (E10/E12) that fallback yields exit 0 clean, a clean verdict derived from evidence that was never read.
Promisor metadata alone proves nothing: a promisor-marked repository whose content is complete must yield the same substantive verdict as its non-promisor twin.

Absence of an object in a promisor-backed repository is unknown, not proved absent: a cited object that is promised but not local is exit 2, while the same object genuinely absent from a non-promisor repository is evidence and yields the ordinary verdict.

measured_base_0df800e.note: the base meets 10 of 14 arms. The four failures are E7, E8, E11 and E14: every arm whose only distinguishing feature is promisor metadata on a content-complete repository. That is the r23 harm, stated as measurable rows. With the metadata stripped from a copy of each fixture, the same fixtures give E7 exit 0 clean (defects 1, corrected 1), E11 exit 0 clean (defects 0, errata_rows 1), E8 exit 1 failed (the E9 counts) and E14 exit 0 clean (defects 1, corrected 1) -- the substantive expectations the candidate must reproduce.

authority.note: expected_after[3] of the original preregistration (a missing citation in any promisor-backed repository is unknown => exit2) was WITHDRAWN prospectively by the live amendment.
